newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly higher in thin trade.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures ended a tad higher on Monday in sparse trade.
Traders said there was very little movement in Euroyen futures as the market lacked fresh factors.
"Share prices moved very little, as did Japanese government bond futures, and this caused Euroyen futures to drift in directionless trade," a trader for a major brokerage house said.
Tokyo share prices would have to stage further rallies for Euroyen futures to be affected, traders said.
A rise above 19,000 on the key Nikkei 225 average on the stock market could invite selling of Euroyen futures, the trader for a major brokerage house said.
Euroyen futures are unlikely to be sold unless the Nikkei 225 rises close to 20,000, a trust bank trader said.
The Nikkei 225 closed at 18,750.65, up 28.65 from Friday"s close. Traders said Euroyen futures are likely to move in a range of about 99.21 to 99.28 in the near term.
The Bank of Japan drained a net 400 billion yen from the money market on Monday, maintaining its neutral stance.

The weighted average of the key overnight call rate was 0.49 percent on Friday.
The key overnight call rate is likely to remain firm at around 0.49 percent in the near future, as short-term fund demand is expected to remain strong, traders said.
No new issues of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were made by late afternoon, traders said.

Three-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent, while about 50 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.54 percent. One-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.52 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from Friday.

Traders said the three-month CD rate was not under much upward pressure, despite the recent maturity of about one trillion yen in three-month CDs. They said a rise in the three-month CD rate based on that factor alone was unlikely.
